Never widen an ignore, add a `skip`/`allow` or silence zizmor to reach green; the one admitted ignore is the Critical CVE response: within 7 days of an advisory confined to a disabled feature, an ignore entry whose reason names that feature (an advisory against an enabled feature: bump the crate within 7 days).

- 2026-11-14: A test-only recorder that replaces every off-list reply with a placeholder also hides why a live step failed: when a recorded live reply comes back refused, read that same granted step's raw reply once by hand before changing the code, then re-record through the recorder.

body:
The session added a Hyprland seam: a new sync library crate, viola-hyprland, that spawns the compositor client hyprctl directly (no shell, no PATH lookup, stdin null) for four JSON queries (clients, activewindow, workspaces, version) and two focus dispatches, then parses each reply through a closed, tolerant parser that drops every text field (titles, classes, names).
Each read is bounded at MAX_FRAME and refused whole as oversize. A child past a provisional 5 s deadline is killed, reaped and reads as unreachable. Every failure is one of five closed code words with a fixed message: unsupported, unreachable, oversize, malformed, refused.
Observability: the hyprctl spawn writes process-start and process-exit with the new subject hyprctl-probe, and a reply it cannot parse writes parse-rejected with the new parser hyprctl-json. The read runs in the span hyprland.read (skip_all), and viola_hyprland joins the viola log targets (7 to 8). No product verb calls the seam yet.
Measured live on Hyprland 0.56.2: dispatch runs as Lua, so the dispatch argv is the Lua focus form, and the only value inserted into it is a closed address or an i32 workspace id.
Test side: a test-only recorder binary, viola-hypr-tap, scrubs each recorded reply to a closed per-request keep-list. The fake agent answers as hyprctl when started under that file name, and a new E2E contract replays the recorded set. A new fuzz target with 9 synthetic seeds was added (fuzz targets 6 to 7), and the new crate is the fifth sync crate under the per-crate tokio ban. Nothing was retired.

body:
The session added a Hyprland seam: a new sync library crate, viola-hyprland, that spawns the compositor client hyprctl directly with a closed argv for four JSON queries (clients, activewindow, workspaces, version) and two focus dispatches, and parses each reply tolerantly into closed types that keep no text field.
The reply read is bounded at MAX_FRAME + 1 bytes and refused whole as oversize. The child gets null stdin, the named env vars removed and a PROVISIONAL 5 s deadline, after which it is killed and reaped. Failures are five closed code words with fixed messages.
Measured live on Hyprland 0.56.2: dispatch runs as Lua, so the plan's dispatch argv was disproved and replaced by hl.dsp.focus forms. The only inserted values are a closed Address newtype or an i32 workspace id.
Added a second test-only recorder (viola-hypr-tap) with a closed per-request string keep-list scrub, a recorded fixture class with its schema and hygiene-walk check, a fake-agent hyprctl personality, a contract test, a fuzz target hyprctl_json, and two new diag-line words: subject hyprctl-probe and parser hyprctl-json.
No product caller yet: the release binary calls none of the seam. No new third-party crate was added. fuzz/Cargo.lock was refreshed after it was found stale.

decision/bounded-readers-census, decision/bounded-external-readers and decision/child-output-bounded: a new bounded child-output reader and a new BOUNDARIES row in the census, with the seam joining the product roots (7 to 8).

decision/upstream-text-is-never-a-command and decision/upstream-text-is-content: the dispatch argv now carries a Lua expression whose only inserted values are a closed Address or an i32. No element is built from reply text and no shell line is built.

decision/statusline-only-shell-out, decision/single-shell-out and decision/statusline-shell-out: a new external child (hyprctl) is spawned directly, with no shell. The statusline stays the only shell-out, but the rule now covers a new spawn.

decision/statusline-deadline and other child-deadline rules: a new PROVISIONAL 5 s HYPRCTL_DEADLINE kills and reaps the child, and a deadline kill reads as unreachable.

body_fields.fact: The Hyprland seam spawns hyprctl directly from a program path its caller resolves. The seam itself does no PATH lookup and reads no environment variable.
The hyprctl reply read is capped at MAX_FRAME + 1 bytes. An over-cap reply is refused whole as oversize before the exit is read, and stderr is drained to MAX_FRAME and dropped.
The hyprctl child runs with null stdin, the named env vars removed and a PROVISIONAL 5 s deadline. It is killed and reaped at the deadline, and a deadline kill or non-zero exit reads as unreachable.

hyprctl dispatch text is a Lua expression (Hyprland 0.56.2 runs dispatch as Lua). Its only inserted values are a closed Address (0x plus 1 to 16 lower-case hex digits) or an i32 workspace id, never reply text, and no shell line is built.

Hyprland fixtures are recorded only through a test-only tap with a closed per-request string keep-list (addresses and the digit version tag). Every other string at any depth is replaced by a placeholder, and a non-JSON reply is kept only when it is the success text ok. The shared scrub and whole refusal follow, and the hygiene walk checks the same keep-list.
The Hyprland reply types hold no text field. Window titles, classes and every other reply string are dropped at the parse and reach no log line and no error.
Hyprland seam failures are five closed words (unsupported, unreachable, oversize, malformed, refused) with fixed messages that interpolate nothing.
